subject: Post-call SLO alignment & test checklist — hosted vs incumbent
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Chen <ops@datamap.ai>, Lena Torres <lena.t@acme.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 28 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call SLO alignment & test checklist — hosted vs incumbent

Hi Oliver / Lena —

Thanks again for taking the time this morning. Quick recap and the concrete asks we agreed during the call so we can scope a hosted verification PoC that maps to your production expectations:

Summary of what we heard from you:
- Medium-volume embeddings + real-time classification on requests that include context blobs (avg payload ~1.6k tokens).
- Current end-to-end targets: p95 ~ 300–350 ms, p99 ~ ~1.0–1.5 s (more below from your ops team).
- Sustained concurrency ~50 r/s, with short bursts to ~200 r/s for ~30s during peak ingestion.
- Streaming is used for long responses to render partial tokens in the client.

Immediate asks / next steps we agreed on:
1) You to share one week of anonymized trace/latency samples and an example request flow (attachment accepted as a small trace JSON). (Oliver)
2) Redwood to propose a pragmatic test plan (synthetic and replay) with endpoints, traffic mix, and measurement windows for p95/p99. (Marcus / Soojin)
3) Agree on a trial window and whether we run on hosted evaluation capacity or a short Dedicated slot. We suggested a 3-day run for steady-state + burst windows. (All)
4) Confirm any strict network egress rules or SNI constraints for your VPC so we can mirror networking in the test. (Procurement/Networking)

I've attached a one-page post-call summary and the list above. If the numbers below are incorrect, feel free to correct in your reply:
- Target p95 end-to-end: 350 ms (incl. client-side parsing + network)
- Target p99 end-to-end: 1.2 s
- Sustained concurrency target: 50 r/s
- Burst: 200 r/s for short periods (~30s)

Proposed dates for the live verification run: March 8–10. If those don't work, suggest alternatives.

Camila
Account Exec | Redwood Inference
camila_reyes@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192
Redwood Inference

From: Oliver Chen <ops@datamap.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>, Lena Torres <lena.t@acme.com>
Date: Sun, 28 Feb 2027 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call SLO alignment & test checklist — hosted vs incumbent

Camila — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming the numbers from our side and attaching a filtered trace sample (anonymized) so you can see end-to-end times we observed last week. Highlights:

- Measured (last 7d production): p95 = 320 ms, p99 = 1.25 s (these are client-observed, include TLS + proxy hops).
- Average request size: ~1.6k tokens; heavy-tail requests up to 6k tokens but rare (~0.5% of traffic).
- Concurrency: steady-state 45–55 r/s; 15–20 bursts/week that spike briefly to 180–220 r/s.
- Streaming: we use partial chunking (WS) with chunk sizes ~250 tokens; UI expects tokens within 120–200 ms after generation.

Attachments: datamap_traces_0227.json, datamap_latency_log.zip

We can provision a small staging key for you to run against mirrored traffic if that helps; otherwise we want to see your proposed test plan and measurement methodology to sign off.

Oliver
Head of Ops — DataMap
ops@datamap.ai | +1 212-555-0147
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Oliver Chen <ops@datamap.ai>, Lena Torres <lena.t@acme.com>
Date: Sun, 28 Feb 2027 12:38:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Post-call SLO alignment & test checklist — hosted vs incumbent

Thanks Camila / Oliver — reviewed the traces. Quick internal plan proposal (high level) so we can align on metrics and instrumentation before booking slots:

Test plan (3-day verification run):
- Day 0 (prep): ingest provided traces, validate request shapes, generate replay harness.
- Day 1 (steady-state): run sustained traffic at 50 r/s for 6 hours, collect p50/p95/p99 (end-to-end) across 60s rolling windows.
- Day 2 (bursts): run scripted bursts to 200 r/s for 30s every 15 minutes for 4 hours to capture queuing/fallback behavior.

Measurement & instrumentation:
- End-to-end measurement points: client -> edge -> model -> client. We'll require a single trace token included in requests so we can correlate.
- Streaming verification: measure token latency from server-generated token to delivery over the WS frame; target 120–200 ms for visible chunk.
- Throughput/cost: we'll run the same workload on our hosted evaluation cluster and provide per-token cost and aggregate throughput numbers.

Requirements from DataMap:
- Please confirm an anonymized trace and one representative large request (6k tokens) so we can test tail behavior.
- Provide any firewall/SNI constraints for staging hosts.

I'll draft a one-page SLO test plan doc and attach (slo_test_plan.md) for your review. If you want a Dedicated short slot for the burst test, call it out and we can put a preliminary reservation.

- Marcus
Principal SRE | Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com

Attachment: slo_test_plan.md
From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Chen <ops@datamap.ai>, Lena Torres <lena.t@acme.com>

Date: Sun, 28 Feb 2027 16:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call SLO alignment & test checklist — hosted vs incumbent

Oliver / Lena —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the traces. Short follow-ups and concrete asks so we can lock calendar and resources:

Action items (we'll own the dates once you confirm):
- DataMap: share the one large request sample (6k tokens) + any staging firewall rules by EOD Wed (Mar 3). (Oliver)
- Redwood: we'll provision a hosted evaluation key and a replay harness. Proposed dry run: Mar 7 (prep), live runs Mar 8–9. If you prefer a Dedicated slot for the burst tests, say so and we'll reserve. (Camila / Marcus)
- Both: confirm whether client-side measurement must include an upstream proxy; we can include proxy hop timing or strip it if you want Redwood-only numbers.

Notes on acceptance criteria (what would count as a pass):
- p95 end-to-end <= 350 ms for steady-state workload (50 r/s).
- p99 end-to-end <= 1.2 s (we'll show both client-observed and Redwood-internal).
- Streaming chunk visibility: first token within 200 ms of generation, and consistent chunk delivery during bursts.
- No more than 2 fallbacks (to lower-cost model variants) per 10k requests during bursts; report any quality regressions.

If those acceptance criteria look good, I'll send the DocuSign pilot agreement + provisional Dedicated reservation (if needed). HubSpot link and DocuSign draft in related links.

Thanks — will await your confirmation on the large sample and any constraints.

Camila
Account Exec | Redwood Inference
